A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BA-solver research. Their complete main texts, Appendices A–E, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison, including material relocated in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation results, component ablations, and qualitative image-editing experiments in Tables 1–3 and 6 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports measured inference-component timings in Appendix E, Table 8.

M1.justification: Appendix E materially revises the reported SideNet architecture: AdaGN, convolutional ResBlocks, and global self-attention are replaced by FiLM, parameter-free Channel RMSNorm, and exclusively depthwise-separable convolutional ResBlocks. This changes the computational structure of the trainable component, although the bi-anchor sampling algorithm, training procedure, and loss remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-conditional ImageNet generation at 256 and 512 resolution and image editing on ImageNet-256. The added timing experiment uses existing ImageNet-256 coverage; no new dataset, domain, or task is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 adds α-flow (Cheng et al., 2025) to the evaluated efficiency comparisons in Tables 2 and 7. Table 7 also explicitly includes the pretrained REPA+SiT base model as a comparator within this comparison. Existing solver and few-step comparator entries are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a runtime-profiling protocol on an NVIDIA H800 with batch size 256 and four-point quadrature, timing one backbone evaluation, four SideNet evaluations, and integration separately. Existing generation metrics, training budgets, sampling settings, and ablation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 8 adds a component-wise efficiency analysis testing how much SideNet and integration overhead contribute to inference latency. The anchor, quadrature-rule, and intermediate-velocity ablations in Table 3, along with the qualitative editing cases, are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its empirical comparisons. The new timing results also lack uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds α-flow FIDs of 2.58, 2.15, and 4.53 at 1, 2, and 8 NFEs, respectively, and a base-model FID of 6.92 at 8 NFEs. Table 8 newly reports 4.1837 seconds for the backbone, 0.2554 for SideNet, 0.0112 for integration, and 4.4502 total. Existing BA-solver scores, ablations, and sample images are retained; the 10-NFE results already appeared in v1 Table 6.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B replace the full-field Lipschitz constant L with an empirically motivated effective residual-drift constant L_eff in the error bounds. This changes the assumptions underlying the bounds, rather than merely notation, while retaining quadratic scaling and the factor-two bi-anchor reduction. Appendix C.3 explicitly states O(h^2) total error alongside the existing O(h^7) quadrature-scheme error.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: lightweight SideNet training, bidirectional temporal perception, bi-anchor integration, high-quality generation with 5–10 NFEs, and image-editing compatibility.

C2.justification: Appendices A–C newly explain performance through partial absorption of state drift and a smaller effective error prefactor, explicitly qualifying the role of high-order quadrature. Section 4.2 newly attributes MeanFlow's degradation at larger NFE budgets to fixed training-time CFG. Appendix E interprets the measured overhead as support for practical acceleration.

D1.justification: Beyond the revised architecture specification, v3 discloses the profiling hardware and batch size, identifies MeanFlow's implementation as a community implementation, and adds training-origin categories and the base model's 250K pretraining iterations in Table 7. Existing hyperparameter Tables 4–5 are unchanged, and no specific community-code access link is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cheng et al. (2025), associated with the new α-flow comparator, and removes the He et al. (2016) ResNet reference. The separately cited AlphaFlow work by Zhang et al. (2025) remains. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the appendix explanations, implementation paragraph, baseline footnote, and efficiency discussion. v3 also adds acknowledgments and author markers and updates the publication footer. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains comparator rows; new Table 7 expands that comparison with a training-type column and additional entries, and Table 8 displays timing components. Figure 1's BATS label becomes BA, Figure 5's caption is shortened, and appendix sample grids move to later pages without changing their images. The overall visual organization is retained.

improvement.justification: The runtime measurements in Table 8 provide direct evidence for the previously asserted small overhead, while Table 7 makes pretraining costs and comparison types more transparent. Explicitly distinguishing total error from quadrature error also improves clarity. These gains are limited: timing covers one configuration, the smaller effective error constant remains heuristic, and the architecture revision is not connected to reruns of the retained benchmark results.
